chunk_map.heading: Acceptance tests catch what a request quietly breaks
Unit tests shrink the agent's room to improvise
TDD keeps intent ahead of the code
Mutation testing checks whether the tests defend anything
Metrics are the dashboard, not the wheel
Small units leave fewer places to hide
Architecture needs an instrument panel too
The human's job moves up, it doesn't vanish
A prompt biases the agent, it does not bind it

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Re-derived post-fix: chunk 5 line 59 now reads 'CRAP pairs a unit's complexity with its test coverage, so a tangled unit with thin tests scores worst. Both expose code that is hard to trust under change.' — 'Both' resolves to CRAP + complexity metrics, both named in the same sentence and the bold lead 'CRAP and complexity metrics.' Maintainer accept-note (line 109) records this as the settled §19/§1 resolution; no pronoun proposed per that note. Checked all other chunks for pronoun/demonstrative antecedents (line 15 'That alone', line 19 'This is the mercury problem', line 23 'this is where', line 67 'it needs instruments', line 63 'This is classic Clean Code') — each resolves against the immediately preceding sentence inside the same chunk. Harm (unresolvable referent) absent everywhere.
No callback to another curriculum file by position anywhere in body; all links are external X citations, named by platform not located by page position.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a standalone supplementary reading, not an exercise/lecture inside a module arc; no 'the X you did/saw' beat references appear anywhere in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal structure anywhere in the file; it is expository practitioner-synthesis prose, not a live-demo beat.
Every ## chunk (1-9) carries a self-contained claim about one named practice plus at least one supporting quote; none is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Closest candidate: chunk 9 header 'A prompt biases the agent, it does not bind it' (line 93) vs. body 'Natural language is not enough. Human language needs formal support: tests, tools, structure, metrics, and feedback loops.' (line 95) — the header's bias/bind framing is a synthesis of that sentence plus the Dijkstra quote rather than a verbatim restatement, but the chunk does not contradict it; it stays inside. All other headers (Acceptance tests / Unit tests / TDD / Mutation testing / Metrics / Small units / Architecture / Human's job) restate their chunk's opening bolded-lead sentence near-verbatim.

No 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' constructions in body prose. Closest candidate for anaphora-triple sub-item: chunk 8 lines 85-91, the verbatim Uncle Bob quote 'Assemblers were faster... Compilers were faster... AIs are faster... Deal with it.' This is an attributed, oEmbed-verified direct quote (source stamp martin-ais-are-faster, line 139) — per dispatch-preamble, altering or flagging a verbatim quote to satisfy a cadence rule would falsify sourced text, so this is reported as a rule question rather than filed REVISE: the triple-parallel structure is Martin's own words, not authored cadence. No self-grading superlatives, no number+retraction shape, no abstraction-noun stacks, no empty-leg verb triplets found elsewhere in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Grepped body for repo/maintainer vocabulary (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, Connections) — none present. 'Steering' is the page's own coined, explicitly-defined thesis term ('So Clean Code becomes steering.' line 27), not repo-internal dialect smuggled onto a slide.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunks 1-8 each carry exactly one bolded handle at the chunk open (**Acceptance Tests.**, **Unit Tests.**, **TDD.**, **Mutation Testing.**, **CRAP and complexity metrics.**, **Small Decoupled Units.**, **Architecture Visibility.**, **Human Mental Model.**), all ≤5 words, consistent with the ≤1-per-slide budget and handle-cap. Chunk 0 and chunk 9 carry zero bold. No whole-sentence bolding anywhere.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: File is a `.../supplementary/*.md` page; maintainer Quality note (line 113-114) records a prior slides@9697944 PASS on this same structural shape and the current session's edit only touched chunk 5's body text, not wrapper/section structure. Not independently re-verified with headless Chrome in this session (no browser tooling run); carried forward as unchanged structurally rather than freshly measured.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
